answer.rationale: Current metrics show simultaneous declines in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory_91 demonstrated that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and drove meaningful action—this directly addresses the activation decline without requiring structural changes. Memory_86 shows onboarding simplification worked, but we're already shortening flows; messaging intervention is orthogonal and can compound those gains. Verification of these two memories will confirm the mechanism and effect sizes from prior work. Promotional pricing (memory_73) addresses competitor pressure but risks margin and doesn't solve the activation/onboarding completion declines. Referral incentives (memory_57) work for established customers but won't help new cohorts currently stuck earlier in the funnel. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is high-value but requires resource allocation beyond a single week's experiment scope. Activation messaging offers the fastest path to reverse the QoQ decline, leverages proven mechanism, and preserves capital for competitive response. Standard_experiment scale allows validated learning without overcommitting to an unproven intervention in a high-pressure week.
